questions.explanation: Scene s1: work = force x distance = 50 x 4 = 200 joules.
questions.prompt: A force of 50 N pushes a crate 4 m in the direction of the force. How much work is done?

choices.text: Correct - the energy is gone once the petrol is finished
Wrong - the energy became heat only, and none of it ever moved the car
Wrong - the energy changed form: chemical energy became kinetic energy plus heat
Wrong - the energy turned back into petrol and leaked away

questions.explanation: The trap is: Energy gets used up when work is done. The car runs out of petrol and stops, so the energy feels destroyed. Energy is never used up: it changes form, like chemical energy becoming kinetic energy plus heat.
questions.misconception: Energy gets used up when work is done.
questions.prompt: A car runs out of petrol and rolls to a stop. A classmate says all its energy has been used up and destroyed. Which statement is correct?

questions.explanation: Scene s2: power = work / time = 200 / 2 = 100 watts.
questions.prompt: The 200 J of work from question 1 is done in 2 s. Calculate the power.

questions.explanation: Scene s3: GPE = m x g x h = 2 x 9.8 x 5 = 98 joules.
questions.prompt: A 2 kg mass is lifted 5 m (g = 9.8 m/s^2). How much gravitational potential energy does it gain?

questions.answer: The 98 J of GPE becomes 98 J of KE; the total energy stays 98 J.
questions.explanation: Scene s3: as the mass falls the GPE drains into KE, and the total stays 98 J - nothing is lost.
questions.prompt: The mass in question 4 falls back to the ground. Describe the energy change, and state the kinetic energy just before it lands, ignoring air resistance.
